correctness.rationale: All metric triangle constraints are necessary and sufficient. The universal lower bound uses the canonical isometric map into the real Lipschitz-free space and averages arbitrary proposed extension values over the exact finite isometry group. The mass-one affine representation gives a single coefficient parameter even for signed maps. Explicit 1-Lipschitz test potentials prove that the optimum cannot improve outside the positive coefficient interval. On that interval, positive transport and distance functions give matching exact bounds (1-(1-k)a)/R and (ell+(1-ell)a)/U. Their monotone intersection and endpoints yield the stated three regimes, all boundary equalities, and norm-one criterion. For verification, 29 finite metrics passed unrestricted-signed-coefficient linear-program comparisons, and the three strict support regimes passed exact-rational examples. These computations do not replace the general proof.

Full relevant sources furnish group averages, general Lipschitz extension bounds, or general finite LP characterizations, but do not give this closed formula. Published two-cluster results inspected instead evaluate internal fluctuation projections, Euclidean distortion, or facets. The known equilateral-source formula does not cover cases with a genuinely shortened intracluster distance. Originality remains a best-knowledge assessment with explicit bibliographic risks.

value.rationale: The source is the simplest non-equilateral two-level finite ultrametric with two symmetric clusters. Its absolute one-point Banach extension constant is a natural norm/projection invariant not determined by generic existence theorems. The result classifies the full admissible parameter family, proves positive weights are optimal even against signed/nonlinear extensions, locates two sharp support-loss thresholds and gives a necessary and sufficient norm-one region. Explicit rational metric examples realize all three genuinely two-level support regimes with nontrivial factor above one. This is a motivated full classification and structural boundary, not a routine isolated rational LP output.
